question: How is a multidisciplinary care plan different from a plan made by just one health worker?

options.A: It removes the need for nursing assessments completely
options.B: It allows the patient to change medical diagnoses at any time
options.C: It combines insights from various fields into one unified set of goals
options.D: It focuses exclusively on hospital discharge procedures

explanation: You're doing great! A team plan blends nursing, social work, and medical insights so every angle of the patient's health is covered.

question: A lecturer leaves an anatomical chart displayed on the board long after the topic has changed to nursing ethics. What mistake has the lecturer made?

options.A: Poor timing and management of visual distraction
options.B: Failing to check the cost of the material
options.C: Using an inaccurate scientific model
options.D: Selecting a non-projected visual aid

explanation: Leaving media displayed after the discussion has moved on distracts learners and dilutes the focus of the current lesson. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of a variance report in nursing management?

options.A: To calculate individual nurse salaries and performance bonuses
options.B: To assess patient physical recovery rates after surgery
options.C: To determine which medical equipment manufacturers to sue
options.D: To compare budgeted financial targets with actual expenses

explanation: Variance reports show where financial goals were hit or missed, helping managers make smart adjustments for the future.

question: What is the primary purpose of having a surgical patient use an incentive spirometer?

options.A: To pump liquid medicine directly into the throat
options.B: To check the patient's blood pressure levels
options.C: To measure how loudly the patient can talk
options.D: To encourage deep breathing and prevent lung collapse

explanation: Incentive spirometry makes patients take deep, deliberate breaths, keeping their alveoli open and preventing postoperative atelectasis. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for pushing those delicate inner cervical cells outward?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Estrogen is the key player here! High levels of estrogen stimulate the inner cervical cells to grow and push outward onto the surface. Great job remembering your reproductive hormones.

question: What is the primary cause of inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Long-term exposure to environmental toxins
options.B: Severe bacterial infections in early childhood
options.C: Faulty genes passed down from parents
options.D: Nutritional deficiencies during pregnancy

explanation: These conditions stem from genetic mutations inherited through family bloodlines rather than external lifestyle factors. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h1)

question: Which of these details is typically recorded in the stock inventory part of the safety form?

options.A: The personal home address of every patient
options.B: Opening balance and quantities used
options.C: Detailed medical diagnoses of injection recipients
options.D: Daily weather conditions at the facility

explanation: Correct! The stock section is strictly about numbers: what we started with, what we used, and what is left.

question: Why is supportive nursing care more common than using specific antidotes for poisoned patients?

options.A: Antidotes are too expensive to keep stocked in standard hospital wards
options.B: Chemical antidotes only work if the patient has an empty stomach
options.C: Specific antidotes are available for only a small percentage of known toxins
options.D: Supportive care eliminates the need for any laboratory blood testing

explanation: We don't have a magic antidote for most poisons, so excellent supportive nursing care to keep the patient stable is a lifesaver.

question: In antenatal care, what does BPCR stand for?

options.A: Baby Physical Care and Recovery
options.B: Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness
options.C: Basic Physiological Childbirth Routine
options.D: Blood Pressure and Cardiac Response

explanation: You've got it! BPCR is all about helping families plan ahead for a normal delivery and know what to do if an emergency pops up.

question: How do azole antifungal drugs stop fungi from growing?

options.A: By stopping the production of essential fungal proteins
options.B: By destroying the genetic material inside the fungal nucleus
options.C: By creating physical holes in the fungal cell wall
options.D: By blocking an enzyme needed to make ergosterol

explanation: Azoles block the factory worker (enzyme) that builds ergosterol. Without ergosterol, the fungus can't maintain its cell wall and dies.

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a straight leg raise test on a patient complaining of back pain?

options.A: To grade the strength of the quadriceps muscle
options.B: To check for spinal nerve root irritation like sciatica
options.C: To measure the exact range of motion of the hip joint
options.D: To test for a torn meniscus inside the knee joint

explanation: Raising the straight leg stretches the sciatic nerve, reproducing radiating pain if a nerve root is compressed or inflamed. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h8)

question: What is the truest way to know if a continuing education training program was actually successful?

options.A: Checking how many participants filled out the seminar evaluation form
options.B: Verifying that all attendees stayed awake throughout the presentation
options.C: Observing if nurses apply what they learned to improve patient bedside care
options.D: Counting how many hours the lecture room lights remained switched on

explanation: Paper evaluations are nice, but real success shows up at the bedside when patients receive better, safer care because of what you learned!

question: A male patient is diagnosed with an indirect inguinal hernia. Which nearby anatomical structure is most at risk of compression within the inguinal canal?

options.A: Spermatic cord contents
options.B: Corporis cavernosa
options.C: Urinary bladder neck
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: Because the spermatic cord passes directly through the inguinal canal, a hernia in this area can compress the vessels and nerves within the cord. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which type of precautions must you use for every single patient, no matter their diagnosis?

options.A: Standard Precautions
options.B: Airborne Precautions
options.C: Reverse Isolation
options.D: Contact Precautions

explanation: Spot on! Standard Precautions are our trusty baseline defense for every patient encounter because we never know an infection's status right away.

question: Why is petroleum jelly (Vaseline) gauze usually placed on the wound after a circumcision?

options.A: To dissolve any remaining surgical stitches instantly
options.B: To speed up the natural growth of pubic hair follicles
options.C: To prevent the raw surgical site from sticking to the diaper
options.D: To permanently numb the glans penis against clothing

explanation: Vaseline acts as a gentle, non-stick shield. It keeps the tender healing skin from sticking painfully to the baby's diaper.

question: In the PDSA cycle, during which phase does the nurse actually carry out the proposed change on a small scale?

options.A: Act phase
options.B: Plan phase
options.C: Study phase
options.D: Do phase

explanation: Keep it up! The 'Do' phase is where you roll up your sleeves and try out the new idea on a small scale to see how it feels in practice.

question: What can happen if strong corticosteroid creams are used on thin skin areas for too long?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the hair follicles
options.B: Skin thinning and atrophy
options.C: Sudden systemic bacterial infection
options.D: Complete numbness of the local nerves

explanation: Using strong steroids for too long breaks down the skin's collagen, causing it to thin out. That's why we always follow prescription timelines carefully!

question: What is a core duty of a community health nurse during immunization outreach?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines locally
options.B: Tracking local child growth charts
options.C: Performing major surgeries
options.D: Ordering hospital meal trays

explanation: Immunization clinics provide a great opportunity for community nurses to screen children and track their growth patterns. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h2)

question: Which type of fever stays consistently high all day with almost no drops?

options.A: Sustained fever
options.B: Remittent fever
options.C: Relapsing fever
options.D: Intermittent fever

explanation: You got it! A sustained fever stays high and steady without giving the patient much of a break throughout the day.

question: Why do clinics use a daily attendance register alongside individual client files?

options.A: To replace the need for client physical examinations
options.B: To store signed legal consent forms permanently
options.C: To quickly summarize daily clinic volume and service types
options.D: To track the personal financial income of clients

explanation: The daily register provides a quick chronological tally of who visited and what was done, which feeds into monthly statistical reports. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h3)

question: What is a major social reason families continue to practice FGM?

options.A: Compliance with international health mandates
options.B: A direct recommendation by the national medical association
options.C: The prevention of childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Fear of social exclusion and unmarriageability

explanation: Sadly, many families do it because they fear their daughters will be rejected by the community or struggle to find husbands. Understanding this helps you treat patients with empathy.

question: Why do hospital-acquired infections matter so much to patient recovery?

options.A: They can delay healing and prolong the hospital stay
options.B: They automatically lower the hospital's electricity bill
options.C: They make hospital rooms look untidy
options.D: They force the hospital to buy more bedsheets

explanation: Infections caught in the hospital add new health complications, making recovery much slower and keeping the patient admitted longer. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h1)

question: What is a simple way nurses can help reduce the emotional burden of isolation?

options.A: Reduce nursing visits so the patient can rest in peace
options.B: Leave the isolation door wide open so the patient can watch the hallway
options.C: Spend time talking with the patient and use video calls to connect with family
options.D: Tell the patient not to worry because isolation is not a big deal

explanation: Active communication and helping the patient stay in touch with loved ones greatly reduces feelings of isolation and depression. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: What is the main role of peer groups during the teenage years?

options.A: Replacing the need for any guidance from healthcare professionals
options.B: Providing a testing ground for independence and social identity away from parents
options.C: Accelerating the physical closure of growth plates in bones
options.D: Eliminating all internal body image anxiety and self-doubt

explanation: Great job! Friends give teenagers a safe space to practice being independent and figure out who they are outside of their families.

question: A nurse wants to know the exact percentage of pregnant women at an antenatal clinic who sleep under treated mosquito nets. What type of question is this?

options.A: Descriptive
options.B: Causal
options.C: Relational
options.D: Interventional

explanation: You got this! Descriptive questions simply paint a picture of what is happening right now in a specific group of people.

question: When caring for someone at the end of life, who do we consider as the true unit of care?

options.A: The hospital ward staff
options.B: The dying patient alone
options.C: The entire family unit
options.D: The attending physician

explanation: In nursing, end-of-life care is never just about the patient alone. We look after the whole family because they share the emotional and psychological journey too!

question: Which of these is NOT a risk factor for spreading an epidemic in a community?

options.A: High vaccination coverage
options.B: Poor solid waste management
options.C: Overcrowded living conditions
options.D: Inadequate clean water supply

explanation: Spot on! High vaccination coverage actually protects a community and stops disease spread, making it the correct exception here.

question: What is the main reason doctors order a skin snip test?

options.A: Detecting dermal microfilariae of Onchocerca volvulus
options.B: Culturing bacterial pathogens in cellulitis
options.C: Measuring deep dermal thickness for burn assessment
options.D: Identifying fungal elements in superficial tinea

explanation: You got this! A skin snip is specifically used to catch tiny parasite larvae (microfilariae) hiding in the skin layers.

question: Which organ needs routine blood test monitoring when a patient is on long-term azole antifungal therapy?

options.A: Thyroid
options.B: Heart
options.C: Lungs
options.D: Liver

explanation: Azole drugs are processed by the liver, so we keep an eye on liver enzymes during long-term therapy to catch any stress early.

question: Which of these is a clear example of objective data?

options.A: A feeling of dizziness upon standing up quickly
options.B: A body temperature reading of 38.5 degrees Celsius
options.C: A statement of anxiety about upcoming surgery
options.D: A patient reporting a dull ache in the lower back

explanation: Objective data is what you can actually see, touch, or measure yourself (like a thermometer reading), unlike feelings that only the patient can tell you about.

question: In SMART goal setting for rehab, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Manual
options.B: Measurable
options.C: Medical
options.D: Maximum

explanation: 'M' stands for measurable! It means you can actually track progress and see how far your patient has come. Easy peasy!

question: How does the tongue help us speak clearly and pronounce words?

options.A: By controlling the rate of air expelled from the lungs
options.B: By opening and closing the lips to form consonants
options.C: By generating vocal cord vibrations in the pharynx
options.D: By altering its shape and position to interrupt and shape oral airflow

explanation: Our tongue is amazingly nimble—it taps against our teeth and palate to turn breath into clear speech and sounds!

question: Which of these is a healthy, adaptive way for a patient to cope with a chronic illness?

options.A: Isolating oneself completely from friends and family
options.B: Seeking social support and talking about their feelings
options.C: Refusing all prescribed medications out of pure frustration
options.D: Pretending that no physical symptoms exist at all

explanation: Reaching out and talking it out helps patients process stress constructively. We all need a support system!

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal mortality?

options.A: Benign breast lumps
options.B: Chronic dental caries
options.C: Uncomplicated malaria
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after childbirth is one of the top direct causes of maternal death worldwide. Knowing how to spot and manage it is essential for every nursing student!

question: Which hormones are mainly responsible for breaking down fat and muscle during the stress of surgery?

options.A: Cortisol and glucagon
options.B: Antidiuretic hormone
options.C: Insulin and estrogen
options.D: Thyroid stimulating hormone

explanation: Well done! Stress hormones like cortisol and glucagon shoot up during surgery to quickly mobilize energy for the body.

question: Which sleep stage is best known for helping the body physically recover and deeply relax its muscles?

options.A: Stage 1 NREM sleep
options.B: Stage 2 NREM sleep
options.C: Stage 3 NREM sleep
options.D: Rapid Eye Movement sleep

explanation: Stage 3 is our deep sleep stage! This is when the body goes to work repairing tissues, building muscle, and healing. Essential for recovery.

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance?

options.A: To continuously track health data and spot where diseases are hiding
options.B: To make cheap medicines for rural clinics
options.C: To diagnose patients with long-term mental illness
options.D: To punish hospitals that miss their cleaning schedules

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on community health trends so we can catch outbreaks before they blow up.

question: What is the main purpose of the National Drug Policy in Nigeria?

options.A: To ensure medicines are safe, effective, and properly used
options.B: To give nurses the sole legal power to write prescriptions
options.C: To make every single medication free for all citizens
options.D: To stop all foreign pharmaceutical companies from importing drugs

explanation: The policy sets standards to protect the public by regulating drug quality, distribution, and rational use. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h1)

question: What does a sudden, significant drop in the baby's heart rate during a contraction usually suggest?

options.A: fetal distress or cord compression
options.B: rapid progression to the second stage
options.C: normal physiological sleep cycles
options.D: maternal exhaustion and dehydration

explanation: Spot on. Big dips in heart rate can mean the baby isn't getting enough oxygen, often due to cord pressure or distress.

question: A patient tells you that both of their parents have high blood pressure and diabetes. Where should you write this?

options.A: Past medical history
options.B: History of present illness
options.C: Review of systems
options.D: Family history

explanation: Spot on! Information about blood relatives (like parents and siblings) always goes into the family history section so you can check for genetic risks.

question: Which of these actions goes against safe infection control practice during venepuncture?

options.A: Recapping used needles using a two-handed technique
options.B: Disposing of the needle directly into a rigid sharps bin
options.C: Performing hand hygiene before putting on clean gloves
options.D: Cleaning the insertion site in a circular outward motion

explanation: Never use two hands to recap a needle! That is a quick way to get an accidental needlestick injury. Always use one hand or drop it straight into the sharps box.

question: What distinct, tough patch does the diphtheria bacterium form in the throat?

options.A: A tough gray pseudomembrane
options.B: A widespread fatty liver
options.C: A fluid-filled skin blister
options.D: A hard calcified granuloma

explanation: Diphtheria creates a stubborn gray coating (pseudomembrane) in the airway made of dead cells, bacteria, and clotting proteins that can block breathing.

question: How are Wernicke encephalopathy and Korsakoff syndrome related?

options.A: They are completely unrelated disorders affecting different organs
options.B: Korsakoff syndrome always occurs years before Wernicke develops
options.C: Wernicke is a mild form of memory loss caused by normal aging
options.D: Wernicke is the acute stage and Korsakoff is the chronic stage

explanation: They are actually two sides of the same coin! Wernicke is the sudden, early emergency phase, and Korsakoff is the long-term memory issue that follows if it's not treated quickly.

question: What does patient autonomy mean in the context of home health care?

options.A: The legal obligation of the family to pay for all medical supplies
options.B: The requirement for patients to live completely independently
options.C: The authority of the nurse to override family member requests
options.D: The right of the patient to make their own choices about care

explanation: Autonomy refers to a patient's right to self-determination and making personal decisions regarding their treatment plan. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is it so important to involve community members during the planning stage of a health program?

options.A: It ensures the program respects local culture and actual needs
options.B: It guarantees that funding will come from international donors
options.C: It removes the need for any evaluation at the end
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid attending community meetings

explanation: When people help plan their own health programs, they take ownership and the project is much more likely to succeed.

question: Which organ in the body is the main factory for producing most of our blood clotting factors?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Liver
options.C: Kidney
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: The liver is a busy chemical plant! It produces almost all the important proteins needed for blood to clot properly.

question: Before opening a standard catheter kit, which major allergies must you always check for?

options.A: Penicillin and sulfa
options.B: Latex and iodine
options.C: Insulin and heparin
options.D: Paracetamol and aspirin

explanation: Always double-check! Standard kits usually contain latex tubing and iodine cleansers, so catching an allergy early saves your patient a lot of pain.

question: What causes standard cramping pain after an abortion?

options.A: Buildup of gas inalos the large intestine
options.B: Contractions of the uterine muscle
options.C: Stretching of the abdominal wall skin
options.D: Infection of the urinary bladder

explanation: You've got this! The uterus naturally squeezes to return to its normal size after a procedure, and those muscular contractions cause period-like cramps. Totally normal part of healing!

question: Where does the lengthwise growth of a long bone happen?

options.A: Periosteal collar
options.B: Medullary cavity
options.C: Epiphyseal plate
options.D: Articular capsule

explanation: You'll hear this called the growth plate! The epiphyseal plate is packed with active cartilage cells that keep pushing bones to grow longer during childhood.

question: What was a major benefit when hospital-based home care programs first started?

options.A: They allowed patients to leave expensive hospital beds earlier while still receiving care
options.B: They completely eliminated the need for outpatient physician clinics
options.C: They removed all financial costs for the patients receiving treatment
options.D: They allowed nurses to perform major surgeries inside private residences

explanation: Extending hospital care into people's homes helped free up expensive hospital beds for sicker patients while keeping costs down.

question: Why should a midwife check her emergency maternity bag on a regular weekly basis?

options.A: To ensure all liquid drugs are transferred into clear glass bottles
options.B: To verify that patient clinical notes are stored inside the drug kit
options.C: To catch expired medications and restock depleted emergency supplies
options.D: To clean the exterior leather surface with strong chemical bleach

explanation: You're thinking like a pro! Regular checks mean you'll never be caught off guard by expired drugs during an emergency.

question: What is the main purpose of United Nations packaging requirements in healthcare?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of shipping medical laboratory supplies
options.B: To speed up the delivery time of routine blood test results
options.C: To ensure all medical specimens look identical to couriers
options.D: To prevent leaks and spills of hazardous materials during transit

explanation: These international rules are designed specifically to contain dangerous biological or chemical contents safely even if the outer box is dropped or crushed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: Why is forcing an exhausted nurse to work a double shift an ethical and legal concern?

options.A: It reduces the amount of paperwork filed in the office
options.B: It always results in immediate promotion for the nurse
options.C: It increases the risk of medical errors and patient harm
options.D: It breaks hospital rules regarding uniform colors

explanation: Exhausted nurses are more prone to mistakes, which threatens patient safety and opens the facility to liability. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h8)

question: What is a key policy step needed to improve medication dispensing systems nationally?

options.A: Making all prescription drugs completely free for every citizen
options.B: Transferring all nursing duties to the central pharmacy department
options.C: Banning the use of mobile carts in all public healthcare facilities
options.D: Including unit dose standards in hospital accreditation requirements

explanation: Enforcing standards through official accreditation ensures hospitals allocate necessary resources to maintain safe dispensing practices. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h8)

question: What happens in the body to make a woman's basal body temperature rise slightly right after ovulation?

options.A: Increased physical activity in the morning
options.B: The release of progesterone
options.C: Dehydration during sleep hours
options.D: A sudden drop in estrogen levels

explanation: Progesterone is a heat-producing (thermogenic) hormone. Once an egg is released, this hormone causes a small, measurable uptick in resting body temperature.

question: Why do UN containers have packing group letters like X, Y, and Z stamped on them?

options.A: To show the degree of hazard and container strength required
options.B: To indicate the specific hospital ward the box originated from
options.C: To list the chemical manufacturer who produced the plastic box
options.D: To tell the courier the exact delivery room temperature needed

explanation: An 'X' rating means the package can handle high-risk items, while 'Y' and 'Z' are for moderate and lower risks. You are mastering the logistics!

question: Which landmark sits right between the front and back fontanelles on a baby's head?

options.A: The mentum
options.B: The vertex
options.C: The base
options.D: The face

explanation: You've got this! The vertex is simply the top part of the head, located right between the two main soft spots (fontanelles).

question: Which of these activities is a core part of the global definition of nursing?

options.A: Filing hospital tax returns and insurance claims
options.B: Promoting healthy lifestyles in local communities
options.C: Purchasing pharmaceutical drugs for wholesale markets
options.D: Designing architectural layouts for new surgical suites

explanation: Nursing goes beyond treating sick people in wards; we also actively promote health and prevent illness right inside our communities! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which part of the brain is your go-to area for balance and coordination?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Brainstem
options.C: Cerebrum
options.D: Spinal cord

explanation: The cerebellum keeps you steady on your feet and helps coordinate your movements so you don't trip over your scrubs! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of glomeruli in the olfactory bulb?

options.A: They destroy excess odorant molecules before transduction occurs
options.B: They physically protect the brain from inhaled bacterial pathogens
options.C: They gather signals from receptors representing the same specific odor type
options.D: They pump mucus across the surface of the nasal epithelium

explanation: You got it! Glomeruli act like sorting hubs, collecting and organizing signals from thousands of similar smell receptors before passing the message along.

question: What is the main goal of giving antiplatelet drugs like aspirin for circulation problems?

options.A: To prevent blood platelets from clumping together and forming clots
options.B: To lower systemic blood pressure by reducing total blood volume
options.C: To dissolve existing large blood clots rapidly in emergency settings
options.D: To widen narrowed blood vessels by relaxing their smooth muscle

explanation: Aspirin and friends act like peacekeepers for your platelets, stopping them from sticking together into stubborn roadblocks inside your blood vessels.

question: What is the biggest hurdle nurses face when handling emergency deliveries in rural community clinics?

options.A: An excessive number of available medical doctors on site
options.B: Lack of immediate access to specialized surgical care and blood banks
options.C: Patients refusing to take prescribed oral medications
options.D: Strict hospital policies preventing any intervention

explanation: Rural clinics often lack advanced surgery and blood supplies, making quick stabilization and fast transfer super important to save lives!

question: What does a survivor-centric approach in nursing care prioritize above all else?

options.A: Public awareness campaigns in local newspapers
options.B: The survivor's rights, wishes, safety, and confidentiality
options.C: The hospital's administrative reporting deadlines
options.D: Immediate arrest of the suspect regardless of consent

explanation: A survivor-centric model puts the autonomy and emotional safety of the patient at the center of every decision. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h6)

question: Why is chronic glomerulonephritis often discovered quite late?

options.A: It develops silently over many years before symptoms show
options.B: Lab tests cannot detect kidney problems early
options.C: Symptoms only appear after dialysis starts
options.D: Patients always ignore early severe pain

explanation: Spot on! The disease moves so slowly that the healthy parts of the kidneys work extra hard to cover for the damaged parts, hiding the problem for a long time.

question: Why do patients with severe metabolic acidosis often end up with high blood potassium?

options.A: Potassium is converted directly into acid inside the liver
options.B: Hydrogen ions move into cells, pushing potassium out into the blood
options.C: Dietary potassium absorption increases during periods of stress
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering blood completely during acid buildup

explanation: To clean up extra acid, cells let hydrogen in, but it acts like a game of musical chairs—forcing potassium out into the blood stream instead!

question: What happens at the end of a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) arrangement?

options.A: The private company permanently owns the hospital building
options.B: The management contract is automatically renewed forever
options.C: The facility is demolished to build commercial real estate
options.D: Ownership of the facility is transferred back to the government

explanation: As the name says, 'BOT' means the private partner builds and runs it for a set time, then hands the keys back to the government!

question: Why does a nurse test tear pH with paper before treating a chemical splash?

options.A: To determine if the patient needs local numbing eye drops first
options.B: To prove that the patient is experiencing a severe allergic reaction
options.C: To measure how severe the chemical exposure is and guide treatment
options.D: To check if the patient has a hidden bacterial eye infection

explanation: Checking the pH tells you if it was an acid or an alkali burn, and you keep washing until the pH goes back to normal. Smart nursing!

question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: To minimize the total cost of obstetric medications
options.B: To ensure all births occur strictly inside tertiary hospitals
options.C: To reduce preventable maternal and newborn deaths
options.D: To completely eliminate pregnancy for high-risk women

explanation: You've got this! Safe motherhood is all about keeping both mum and baby safe and healthy by stopping complications before they get out of hand.

question: What is a common daily challenge for clinical nurses who want to get involved in research?

options.A: Being forced to write books instead of working
options.B: Balancing heavy patient care duties with data collection tasks
options.C: Having too much free time during morning shifts
options.D: Lacking access to any patients in the hospital

explanation: You got it! Ward work is busy, and finding extra time to gather data on top of caring for patients is no small feat.

question: What type of question is best for encouraging a patient to talk freely during a health counselling session?

options.A: Closed yes-or-no question
options.B: Leading accusation question
options.C: Strictly rhetorical question
options.D: Open-ended question

explanation: Open-ended questions (like "How do you feel about...?") give clients the floor to share their true thoughts instead of just nodding with a quick yes or no.

question: Why are mums who had a very long, exhausting labour at high risk of heavy bleeding after birth (PPH)?

options.A: Her exhausted uterine muscle fails to contract firmly to seal off bleeding blood vessels.
options.B: The placenta always remains completely attached inside the uterus forever.
options.C: Her body stops producing all platelets during the second stage of labour.
options.D: Her blood pressure naturally drops to zero immediately after delivery.

explanation: Correct! Think of the uterus like a muscle that just ran a marathon—by the end, it's too tired to clamp down tightly and shut off the bleeding vessels (uterine atony).

question: Why do we really need home-grown, local nursing research data in Nigeria?

options.A: Strict penalties for hospitals that do not run clinical trials
options.B: Government regulations forcing every nurse to publish a book
options.C: The desire of international pharmaceutical companies to sell drugs
options.D: The need for evidence that reflects regional and cultural realities

explanation: Brilliant! Textbook solutions from abroad don't always fit our local environment. We need research that speaks directly to our specific communities and resources.

question: When reading a skin test, which specific physical change should you measure?

options.A: Erythema
options.B: Temperature
options.C: Ecchymosis
options.D: Induration

explanation: You nailed it! We measure induration (the hard, raised bump) because that shows a true immune response, whereas simple surface redness doesn't mean a positive result.

question: What is the core idea behind cultural competence in nursing?

options.A: Refusing to treat patients who consult traditional healers
options.B: Speaking only English during all patient health education sessions
options.C: Forcing patients to abandon their native beliefs in favor of modern science
options.D: Respecting patient traditions while promoting safe and effective health practices

explanation: Exactly! Cultural competence means honoring where our patients come from and blending their values with safe, evidence-based nursing care.

question: What is a medical compress?

options.A: A clean, moist cloth applied to a specific body area
options.B: An airtight plastic sheet wrapped around a limb
options.C: A dry heating pad placed over unbroken skin
options.D: A tight bandage used to stop severe external bleeding

explanation: Think of a compress as a simple, clean, wet cloth placed right on the skin to give warm or cool therapy where it's needed most. Spot on!

question: What is another common name for therapeutic dietary counselling?

options.A: Holistic wellness education
options.B: Preventive lifestyle coaching
options.C: Medical nutrition therapy
options.D: General community wellness

explanation: Therapeutic counselling uses specific food and nutrient adjustments to treat active illnesses, which is known as medical nutrition therapy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h4)

question: What is the main public health goal of giving vaccines to lots of people in a community?

options.A: To treat active bacterial infections in hospitalized patients
options.B: To interrupt transmission cycles and prevent infectious diseases
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for personal hygiene
options.D: To replace the body's natural immune system entirely

explanation: You got this! Vaccines train our immune systems to stop germs in their tracks before they can spread through a whole neighborhood.

question: Why is a continuous supply of nutrients necessary for human tissues?

options.A: Cells constantly carry out metabolic processes requiring fuel
options.B: The digestive tract stops working without fresh food hourly
options.C: Stored nutrients last for only a few minutes in the body
options.D: Tissues constantly expand in size throughout adult life

explanation: Cells never truly rest; they continually perform work that demands a steady influx of nutrients and energy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h1)

question: What was the major pharmacological breakthrough made by Friedrich Sertürner in 1805?

options.A: Synthesizing aspirin in a laboratory
options.B: Inventing the first hypodermic syringe
options.C: Isolating pure morphine from opium
options.D: Discovering penicillin from a mold

explanation: Friedrich Sertürner isolated morphine from opium, which marked the historical first extraction of an active pure chemical compound from a medicinal plant. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h4)

question: How do opioids cause dangerous breathing slowdowns (respiratory depression) during an overdose?

options.A: By blocking receptors in the brainstem that control breathing
options.B: By physically blocking air from entering the trachea
options.C: By paralyzing the muscles in the hands and arms
options.D: By causing the lung tissue to fill with fluid instantly

explanation: Opioids target the control center in the brainstem, effectively dampening the body's natural urge to breathe. This is why monitoring breathing is always top priority!

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for a patient going into shock from severe post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: Perform a detailed psychosocial history regarding the pregnancy
options.B: Send the patient immediately for diagnostic pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Administer oral rehydration salts and counsel on contraception
options.D: Insert large-bore intravenous lines for fluid resuscitation

explanation: ABC comes first—and in bleeding shock, getting IV lines open fast to pump fluids and restore blood volume is an absolute lifesaver! You've got this.

question: Which of these is considered an extrinsic cause of a restrictive lung disease?

options.A: Chronic bronchitis from smoking
options.B: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
options.C: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
options.D: Severe scoliosis of the spine

explanation: You're doing awesome. 'Extrinsic' means the problem is outside the lung tissue itself—like a curved spine (scoliosis) squeezing the chest wall. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why do we often describe the pelvic floor as a hammock?

options.A: It swings freely between the hips to cushion the baby's head
options.B: It stretches from the pubic bone to the coccyx to support pelvic organs
options.C: It hangs loosely from the abdominal wall to protect the intestines
options.D: It attaches only to the hip joints to assist with walking

explanation: Great thinking! Just like a hammock, these muscles stretch right from front to back to cradle the bladder, uterus, and bowels.

question: Which household item is a very common fall hazard for an elderly home care patient?

options.A: Bright overhead lighting in the main hallway
options.B: Loose scatter rugs on polished wooden floors
options.C: Sturdy wooden handrails installed along a staircase
options.D: A heavy armchair placed firmly against a corner wall

explanation: Spot on! Those pretty little scatter rugs love to slide underfoot or catch walking aids like canes. Removing them is an easy win for home safety.

question: Which of these is a structural (physical) part of a community?

options.A: General trust among local neighbors
options.B: The overall happiness of the population
options.C: The speed of municipal emergency response
options.D: Geographical location and housing conditions

explanation: Great job! The physical structure refers to what you can actually see and map out, like houses, roads, and the location itself.

question: How does a functional drug classification differ from a therapeutic one?

options.A: It focuses strictly on the financial cost of the medication
options.B: It describes how the drug works at a cellular or physiological level
options.C: It dictates the preferred route of administration for the nurse
options.D: It lists only the herbal ingredients found in traditional remedies

explanation: While therapeutic class tells you the disease treated, functional class explains the exact body process or cellular mechanism the drug alters.

question: What is the very first link in the adult chain of survival?

options.A: Early recognition and call for help
options.B: Immediate high-quality chest compressions
options.C: Rapid use of an automated external defibrillator
options.D: Advanced life support by paramedics

explanation: Recognizing an emergency and activating the emergency response system quickly starts the entire rescue process. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which nursing theory focuses heavily on helping a person or community practice self-care?

options.A: Florence Nightingale's Environmental Theory
options.B: Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Sigmund Freud's Psychosexual Theory
options.D: Abraham Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs

explanation: Spot on! Orem's model is all about empowering people with the skills they need to take charge of their own health.

question: What is a major perk of delaying cord clamping for a healthy newborn?

options.A: It increases iron stores and placental blood transfer
options.B: It makes cutting the umbilical cord much easier for the nurse
options.C: It prevents the baby from developing neonatal jaundice
options.D: It speeds up the expulsion of the placenta from the uterus

explanation: Waiting just a bit before clamping lets that extra, valuable blood flow right from the placenta into the baby, protecting them against early anemia.

question: How do drug name stems help a student nurse understand unfamiliar medications?

options.A: They show the exact expiration date and proper storage temperature needed
options.B: They tell the nurse the exact retail price of the medication in the pharmacy
options.C: Common suffixes reveal the pharmacological class and general action of the drug
options.D: They indicate which manufacturing company produced the specific batch of pills

explanation: Drug stems (like '-olol' for beta-blockers) are like cheat codes! They tell you what family a drug belongs to, helping you guess its action even if you've never seen it before.

question: How does increased blood flow help an infected, swollen area under a poultice?

options.A: It dries out all body fluids completely
options.B: It cools down the fever instantly
options.C: It brings white blood cells to fight the infection
options.D: It stops the heart from pumping too fast

explanation: Extra blood circulation delivers necessary white blood cells and nutrients to heal inflamed or infected tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h2)

question: When is it legally okay for a nurse to share a patient's private medical diagnosis with someone else?

options.A: When a curious neighbor asks about the patient's illness.
options.B: When the nurse wants to discuss interesting cases on social media.
options.C: When the hospital manager asks casually out of curiosity.
options.D: When required by statute or public health laws for specific diseases.

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred, but the law allows exceptions when reporting public health threats (like certain infectious diseases or gunshot wounds) to the appropriate authorities.

question: Why are regular walkthrough inspections so important for an occupational health nurse?

options.A: To discipline workers who fail to wear proper uniforms
options.B: To check the financial profits of the plant
options.C: To replace safety officers during their annual leave
options.D: To observe daily work tasks and identify unaddressed environmental risks

explanation: Exactly! Walking through the workspace lets you spot hidden dangers that workers might just get used to and forget to report.

question: What usually causes antimicrobial resistance to spread in clinical practice?

options.A: Using combination drug therapy for mycobacterial infections
options.B: Regular handwashing and proper cleaning of hospital equipment
options.C: Administering culture-guided targeted therapy to patients
options.D: Inappropriate use and incomplete courses of anti-infective drugs

explanation: Misusing antibiotics—like taking them for viral colds or stopping halfway—teaches bacteria how to survive our best drugs. Good hand hygiene and smart prescribing protect everyone!

question: A patient comes to the emergency ward bleeding heavily from an unsafe abortion. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Provide immediate lifesaving emergency care to stabilize the patient
options.B: Report the patient to the police before offering any medical treatment
options.C: Wait for a court order before administering intravenous fluids
options.D: Refuse care based on personal moral objections to abortion

explanation: Saving a life always comes first! As a nurse, your duty is to stabilize and treat your patient in an emergency, no matter the circumstances. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: A nurse accidentally gives the wrong dose because two different drugs have almost identical labels. In a Just Culture, how is this viewed?

options.A: Intentional harm requiring criminal investigation
options.B: Human error requiring system and package redesign
options.C: At-risk behavior requiring strict disciplinary suspension
options.D: Reckless behavior requiring immediate termination

explanation: Spot on! Confusing look-alike labels is an innocent human slip. Instead of blaming the nurse, a Just Culture fixes the faulty packaging so it doesn't happen again.

question: What should you do immediately if mixed medications inside a syringe driver turn cloudy?

options.A: Vigorously shake the syringe to dissolve the cloudy particles back in
options.B: Leave the pump running because color changes are completely normal
options.C: Increase the infusion rate to push the cloudy solution through faster
options.D: Discard the mixture immediately because the drugs are likely incompatible

explanation: Well done! Cloudiness means a chemical reaction happened between the drugs, making them unsafe. Never give a cloudy mixture—always prepare a fresh, safe set.

question: Which lab test is best for checking the body's stored iron over time?

options.A: Serum ferritin
options.B: Total white cell count
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Serum sodium

explanation: Serum ferritin measures the iron tucked away in your body's savings account (stores), making it the top choice for tracking true iron recovery.

question: A community nurse shares treated mosquito nets during a malaria surge. Which part of the epidemiological triangle is this targeting?

options.A: The internal incubation period
options.B: The host's genetic makeup
options.C: The infectious agent directly inside the blood
options.D: The environment

explanation: Nets change the surroundings where humans and mosquitoes meet, which means we are modifying the environment to block transmission.

question: How does aldosterone help raise blood pressure once it is released during the RAAS cascade?

options.A: It forces the heart to beat much faster
options.B: It causes the kidneys to retain sodium and water
options.C: It relaxes blood vessels throughout the body
options.D: It triggers the thirst center in the brain

explanation: Aldosterone signals the renal tubules to reabsorb sodium, pulling water along with it to increase blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which safety rule is absolute when a patient is using home oxygen therapy?

options.A: Using petroleum jelly freely around the nose to prevent dryness
options.B: Placing heavy wool blankets over the oxygen concentrator
options.C: Connecting the machine to a cheap extension cord
options.D: Prohibiting open flames and smoking near the oxygen source

explanation: Oxygen fuels fire! Even a tiny spark or open flame near oxygen can trigger a fast, dangerous blaze.

question: What is the main job of the endocrine system in our body?

options.A: Defending the body against foreign pathogens
options.B: Regulating body functions through hormone secretion
options.C: Filtering waste products directly from the bloodstream
options.D: Providing structural support for internal organs

explanation: Think of the endocrine system as your body's chemical messaging network! It uses glands to release hormones straight into the blood, controlling everything from growth to metabolism. You've got this!

question: What kind of diet is best for a patient recovering from enteric fever to protect their gut?

options.A: Soft, low-fiber diet
options.B: High-fiber whole grain diet
options.C: High-residue raw vegetable diet
options.D: Raw meat and dairy diet

explanation: Well done! A soft, low-fiber diet is gentle on the tummy and avoids irritating the healing intestinal walls.

question: Testing for the HLA-B*5701 genetic variant helps prevent which serious issue?

options.A: Sudden kidney failure caused by common diuretics
options.B: Chronic high blood pressure from oral contraceptives
options.C: Severe hypersensitivity reactions to abacavir
options.D: Severe internal bleeding during anticoagulant therapy

explanation: Well remembered! Checking for the HLA-B*5701 allele protects patients from having a dangerous, sometimes life-threatening allergic reaction to the HIV drug abacavir. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the single biggest risk factor for breast cancer that you cannot change?

options.A: Engaging in sedentary office work
options.B: Being female and advancing in age
options.C: Living in a densely populated city
options.D: Consuming a high-fat urban diet

explanation: Simply growing older and being a woman carry the highest statistical risk. It's totally unmodifiable, but knowing it helps us target our screening!

question: What two main elements make up the foundation of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Art and science
options.B: Administration and finance
options.C: Theory and politics
options.D: History and geography

explanation: Nursing combines the emotional and human connection of art with the empirical clinical knowledge of science to care for patients effectively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: What infection prevention practice is most important when inserting a contraceptive implant under the skin?

options.A: Giving the patient general anesthesia
options.B: Using strict aseptic (sterile) technique
options.C: Making the patient fast for 12 hours
options.D: Using ultraviolet room lights

explanation: Spot on! Even though it's a minor procedure, keeping everything strictly sterile protects your patient from nasty wound infections.

question: Why do we use a Gram stain when looking at a bacterial colony under the microscope?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the bacterial sample on a scale
options.B: To freeze the microorganisms so they can be stored for years
options.C: To provide extra nutrients for the bacteria to grow faster
options.D: To categorize the bacteria by their cell wall structure and color

explanation: Gram staining is a classic nursing and lab trick! It sorts bacteria into neat groups based on how their cell walls react to the violet dye.

question: A newly admitted patient is shaking before a scheduled biopsy. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Frustration over wearing a standard hospital gown
options.B: Disappointment with the hospital meal schedule
options.C: Anticipation of pain and uncertainty about the diagnosis
options.D: Annoyance with noisy roommates in the ward

explanation: You're right! Not knowing what the results will be, coupled with the worry of physical pain, is a classic recipe for procedure anxiety.

question: Why is it so vital to write down moulding details accurately on the partograph?

options.A: It proves that the nurse gave pain medication at the correct time
options.B: It replaces the need to check the fetal heart rate during the second stage
options.C: It serves as a legal receipt for the hospital fees charged to the patient
options.D: It gives the healthcare team a clear visual trend of whether labour is becoming obstructed

explanation: The partograph gives everyone a quick visual story of how labour is going, helping the whole shift spot dangerous trends before they become emergencies.

question: Why must nurses be careful when giving cimetidine to patients taking many other drugs?

options.A: It completely stops the liver from filtering blood entirely
options.B: It immediately destroys all other oral medications in transit
options.C: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in every patient
options.D: It is known to cause many drug interactions in the body

explanation: Cimetidine interacts with liver enzymes, which can change how other medications are processed in the body. Always double-check drug guides!

question: A patient has an injury damaging the nerve fibers in their ventral root. What would you expect to see?

options.A: Inability to move the target muscle effector
options.B: Inability of receptors to detect hot temperatures
options.C: Loss of sensation to pinprick in the skin
options.D: Total loss of conscious thought and memory

explanation: Since the ventral root carries the outgoing 'action' command to muscles, damaging it blocks that final signal, leading to weakness or trouble moving.

question: Why is setting up an IV line so crucial during a resuscitation?

options.A: To secure the endotracheal tube in place
options.B: To measure the exact volume of carbon dioxide exhaled
options.C: To monitor the patient's core body temperature
options.D: To deliver emergency medications and fluids directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Spot on! An IV line acts like a fast highway to pump life-saving drugs straight into circulation when every second counts. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which of these is a key community role for a nurse promoting safe motherhood?

options.A: Manufacturing routine pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Managing hospital financial budgets
options.C: Performing major obstetric surgeries alone
options.D: Health education and mobilizing families

explanation: You got it! Teaching families about danger signs and encouraging them to visit the clinic early is one of our best community tools.

question: Which Nigerian food item is an excellent local source of both plant protein and healthy fats?

options.A: Melon seeds (egusi)
options.B: Refined white sugar
options.C: Packaged soft drinks
options.D: Polished white garri

explanation: Spot on! Egusi is packed with valuable plant proteins and healthy fats, making it a powerhouse for local nutrition.

question: Which of the following is a major limitation of non-experimental research?

options.A: Excessive control over the natural hospital environment
options.B: Impossibility of using statistical analysis
options.C: Unethical manipulation of patient treatment plans
options.D: Inability to definitively establish cause and effect

explanation: Great thinking! Because we aren't controlling every single outside factor or changing variables on purpose, we can't say for sure that one thing caused another.

question: What actually is sepsis?

options.A: The initial stage of viral reproduction in a host cell
options.B: A localized skin reaction caused by fungal overgrowth
options.C: A systemic, life-threatening response to an infection
options.D: A normal immune reaction during the prodromal phase

explanation: Correct! Sepsis happens when an infection gets out of hand, triggering a severe, dangerous full-body inflammatory response that needs emergency care.

question: What is the main job of GnRH agonist medications when treating endometriosis?

options.A: To dissolve existing pelvic scar tissue and adhesions
options.B: To stimulate rapid ovulation and increase fertility chances
options.C: To permanently increase the secretion of progesterone from the adrenal glands
options.D: To suppress estrogen production and shrink endometrial implants

explanation: These drugs put the body into a temporary 'pause' state by blocking estrogen. Without estrogen fueling them, the misplaced tissue patches shrink away.

question: How do high-grade cancer cells usually act compared to low-grade cancer cells?

options.A: High-grade cells never metastasize to lymph nodes.
options.B: High-grade cells are easier to destroy with basic antibiotics.
options.C: High-grade cells look identical to healthy tissue under a lens.
options.D: High-grade cells grow and spread much more rapidly.

explanation: High-grade cells are fast-growing and more aggressive, meaning doctors need to act quickly. You're doing great learning this!

question: How do painful abscesses and bacterial infections usually happen after an injection?

options.A: Due to the natural chemical reaction of the medication inside the blood
options.B: As a normal side effect of every vaccine given in the muscle
options.C: Because the patient did not take oral antibiotics before the injection
options.D: Through contaminated equipment or poor skin preparation introducing bacteria

explanation: Abscesses happen when germs get introduced into the skin or muscle. This is why thorough hand washing, clean gear, and proper skin wiping are so important!

question: Which of the following is NOT a systemic risk associated with unsafe or unnecessary injections?

options.A: Systemic complications from contaminated equipment
options.B: Transmission of Hepatitis B and C viruses
options.C: Development of complete tolerance to oral painkillers
options.D: Acquisition of secondary bloodstream infections

explanation: Unsafe injections cause infections and bloodborne virus transmission, not oral drug tolerance. The question asks for what is NOT a risk. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: During which phase of the nurse-patient relationship do you first build trust and set professional boundaries?

options.A: The termination phase
options.B: The working phase
options.C: The pre-interaction phase
options.D: The orientation phase

explanation: The orientation phase is your official 'meet and greet' where you introduce yourself, set ground rules, explain your roles, and start building that vital therapeutic trust.

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of bringing health insurance into the DRF model?

options.A: It provides a secondary stream of income for purchasing drugs
options.B: It helps spread healthcare financial risks across a larger population
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any initial seed capital
options.D: It protects patients from paying high cash prices out of pocket

explanation: Correct! Insurance brings in great ongoing funds, but you still need that initial stock or cash to get the pharmacy doors open in the first place.

question: What is the main goal of home health care?

options.A: To provide permanent housing for chronically ill elderly citizens
options.B: To train family members to take over all doctor responsibilities
options.C: To deliver professional nursing and medical services directly to a patient's residence
options.D: To completely replace the need for emergency room visits during major trauma

explanation: Spot on! Home health care brings clinical nursing straight to the patient's doorstep to help them heal comfortably where they live.

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to break patient confidentiality?

options.A: When a curious coworker asks about a patient's diagnosis
options.B: When family members demand updates over the telephone
options.C: When the nurse wants to gossip about a famous admission
options.D: When the patient poses an immediate danger to self or others

explanation: Well done! Safety always comes first—if someone is in immediate danger of harm, confidentiality rules can be bypassed to keep people safe.

question: Why is regular walking encouraged for patients with stable peripheral artery disease?

options.A: It forces venous blood upward by squeezing calf muscles
options.B: It helps tiny new blood vessels (collateral vessels) grow around blockages
options.C: It melts away calcified plaque in the leg arteries
options.D: It lowers heart rate and stops vasospasms

explanation: Exercise stimulates the body to build little detour pathways around blocked arteries! These collateral vessels bring fresh oxygen to leg muscles over time.

question: What is a key role of a nurse acting as a community champion for reproductive health?

options.A: Writing national health insurance budget laws
options.B: Replacing traditional village chiefs in council meetings
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical contraceptive drugs
options.D: Educating and advocating outside hospital walls

explanation: Community champions extend their reach into local spaces to educate populations and advocate for better health practices. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: Why can the withdrawal method fail to prevent pregnancy even when the man pulls out on time?

options.A: Pre-ejaculatory fluid may contain active sperm
options.B: Urine mixes with semen inside the bladder
options.C: Semen can absorb through the skin of the thigh
options.D: Vaginal walls produce their own sperm cells

explanation: Pre-cum released during excitement can pick up leftover sperm waiting in the urethra, introducing them into the vagina before the actual pull-out.

question: Which of these everyday lifestyle habits can negatively impact fertility in both men and women?

options.A: Natural age-related decline
options.B: Genetic chromosome makeup
options.C: Congenital uterine anomalies
options.D: Cigarette smoking

explanation: Brilliant! Smoking is a habit patients can actually change, and it directly hurts both sperm quality and ovarian health. You're mastering this!

question: What is a major advantage of Rapid Diagnostic Tests in primary health care?

options.A: They provide quick results with minimal equipment
options.B: They eliminate the need for clinical history taking
options.C: They are completely free to manufacture worldwide
options.D: They never give false results

explanation: RDTs are designed to give fast answers at the bedside or in remote clinics without needing heavy laboratory machinery. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why does effective planning help reduce chaos on a hospital ward?

options.A: By eliminating all unexpected medical admissions to the facility
options.B: By allowing nurses to ignore hospital policies during emergencies
options.C: By anticipating patient needs and mapping out required resources ahead of time
options.D: By transferring all administrative duties directly to junior student nurses

explanation: Looking ahead allows managers to prepare staff and supplies before a crisis hits, keeping the ward calm and orderly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h1)

question: In the ward, what do we call a non-living object—like a BP cuff or a table—that can transfer germs?

options.A: A living insect that transmits a parasite to humans
options.B: A type of protective mask worn during surgery
options.C: An inanimate object that can transfer infectious agents
options.D: An antibiotic resistant strain of hospital bacteria

explanation: That's a fomite! Any non-living surface or object that picks up germs and passes them to the next patient is a fomite.

question: Which part of the nervous system includes the sensory nerves branching out to your skin and organs?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Peripheral nervous system
options.C: Autonomic sympathetic chain
options.D: Enteric digestive network

explanation: You got it! Think of the central nervous system as the main office (brain and spinal cord), while the peripheral nervous system is the field crew reaching out to every corner of the body.

question: How do patients usually move through the stages of dying?

options.A: Rapidly within the first twenty-four hours of a diagnosis
options.B: Always starting with depression and ending with anger
options.C: Fluidly, often moving back and forth or skipping steps
options.D: Strictly one after the other in a neat timeline

explanation: Grief is never a straight line. Patients often bounce back and forth or skip steps entirely, and that is completely normal!

question: What is the bed elevation angle for a patient in the semi-Fowler's position?

options.A: Exactly 90 degrees
options.B: 60 to 75 degrees
options.C: 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: 15 to 30 degrees

explanation: Semi-Fowler's raises the head of the bed moderately, usually between 30 and 45 degrees, to aid breathing. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h4)

question: What does the glycemic index (GI) measure about a carbohydrate food?

options.A: The amount of sodium added during processing
options.B: How much total fiber is in the serving
options.C: How fast and high it raises blood sugar
options.D: The exact number of calories it contains

explanation: The glycemic index ranks foods by their speed and intensity in raising blood glucose levels. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h3)

question: How does poverty in a specific region usually affect the health of the people living there?

options.A: Economic poverty has no effect on maternal or child mortality rates
options.B: Poor economic areas generally have worse health indicators and fewer resources
options.C: Rural areas with low income receive more government funding than cities
options.D: Deprived regions always have better health outcomes due to less pollution

explanation: Where there is poverty and lack of infrastructure, health statistics like maternal and child survival tend to suffer.

question: A nurse notices a 16-year-old girl repeatedly visiting the clinic for minor injuries with vague explanations. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Scold the patient for being clumsy and failing to take proper precautions
options.B: Report the parents immediately to law enforcement without talking to the teen
options.C: Conduct a private psychosocial assessment using a structured tool like HEADSS
options.D: Discharge the patient quickly so other acute emergency cases can be seen

explanation: Correct! Repeated, unexplained injuries are a major red flag. A private, gentle interview using a tool like HEADSS helps uncover abuse or emotional distress.

question: What is the main goal of striving for health equity in our communities?

options.A: Eliminating all private hospitals in the healthcare sector
options.B: Ensuring equal funding for all urban medical centers
options.C: Ensuring everyone has a fair opportunity to achieve good health
options.D: Providing identical medical treatments to every single person

explanation: Exactly right! Health equity means clearing away unfair barriers so that everyone, no matter their background, has a fair shot at being healthy.

question: What should a nurse do first when meeting a vulnerable family for an assessment?

options.A: Threaten to report them to social services if they refuse to talk
options.B: Focus only on their financial debts
options.C: Build trust and create a friendly, non-judgmental atmosphere
options.D: Tell them how to manage their personal money

explanation: Spot on! Families need to feel respected and safe before they will open up about their struggles and accept your nursing help.

question: What is a common long-term effect specifically linked to removing the clitoris?

options.A: Permanent closure of the vaginal canal
options.B: Complete paralysis of the lower extremities
options.C: Chronic loss of sensory and sexual function
options.D: Continuous production of excess amniotic fluid

explanation: Correct! Because the clitoris has many sensitive nerve endings, removing it leads to lasting sensory changes and distress.

question: What is a major challenge facing families who seek formal custodial care in urban Nigerian cities?

options.A: High out-of-pocket costs because insurance rarely covers non-medical care
options.B: Strict government laws that forbid hiring private home caregivers
options.C: Complete lack of any individuals willing to work as caregivers
options.D: An overabundance of free public nursing homes in every neighborhood

explanation: Because health insurance typically covers acute medical care rather than long-term custodial help, families must pay out of pocket for private aides. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why is family involvement important during the discharge planning process?

options.A: Relatives need to drive the nursing staff home after their shift ends
options.B: Family members often provide ongoing care and support at home
options.C: Family members must clean the hospital bed before the next patient arrives
options.D: Relatives are legally required to sign the hospital utility bills

explanation: Involving family ensures that the people assisting the patient at home understand medication routines, warning signs, and necessary lifestyle changes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: What happens in the nervous system when an opioid binds to its receptor?

options.A: It forces the body to release high amounts of natural prostaglandins
options.B: It stimulates rapid electrical firing along nerve endings
options.C: It inhibits the transmission of pain signals to the brain
options.D: It speeds up the heart rate to increase oxygen delivery

explanation: Think of opioids as a roadblock: they stop pain messages from traveling up the nerves so your brain doesn't feel them as intensely.

question: Which of the following is an example of demographic data?

options.A: Common cultural beliefs about healing
options.B: The number of available hospital beds
options.C: The pH level of the local drinking water
options.D: Age distribution and population size

explanation: Demographics focus on the statistical characteristics of human populations, such as age, size, and sex distribution. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary function of a pulse oximeter?

options.A: To count the exact white blood cell count
options.B: To estimate blood oxygen saturation
options.C: To check the amount of carbon dioxide in the lungs
options.D: To measure blood pressure levels

explanation: Pulse oximetry is specifically designed to non-invasively measure the percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin in the blood. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h1)

question: In waste management, what does the term 'leachate' mean?

options.A: The gas that builds up inside sealed biological waste autoclaves
options.B: Contaminated liquid that drains from waste dumps into soil and water sources
options.C: Protective fluid applied to gloves before handling sharp objects
options.D: A special chemical spray used to clean medical instrument trays

explanation: You got it! When rainwater trickles through poorly stored waste, it picks up nasty chemicals and germs, forming 'leachate' that can pollute underground water.

question: A patient discharged after treatment for nephrotic syndrome calls the clinic reporting a new, warm, swollen, and painful calf. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Normal muscle recovery after being on bed rest
options.B: An allergic reaction to the prescribed diuretic
options.C: Rapid healing of the kidney filtration barrier
options.D: A deep vein thrombosis due to protein loss

explanation: Unilateral calf pain and swelling in a patient with nephrotic syndrome is a classic red flag for a deep vein thrombosis caused by altered clotting factors. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h7)

question: During a routine check, what does a pale, dusky, or blue-purple stoma tell you?

options.A: Inadequate blood supply to the stoma tissue
options.B: Normal healing after belly surgery
options.C: Too much fluid intake by the patient
options.D: A properly sealed ostomy appliance

explanation: Spot on. Color changes like blue, purple, or paleness mean blood flow is blocked or low—this is a true surgical emergency!

question: How does social media help spread harmful diet trends?

options.A: It forces government agencies to approve new superfoods daily.
options.B: It lowers the market cost of rare and exotic dietary supplements.
options.C: It creates virtual communities that make strict rules feel rewarding.
options.D: It provides rigorous peer-reviewed data from medical doctors.

explanation: Online groups make people feel like they belong to a special team when they follow harsh diet rules together. Keep up the great study flow!

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain?

options.A: 31 pairs
options.B: 24 pairs
options.C: 12 pairs
options.D: 8 pairs

explanation: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves that connect the brain directly to various structures mostly located in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: Student nurses are preparing an outreach during the rainy season when cholera is common. What should they bring?

options.A: Bring water purification and cholera prevention flipcharts to demonstrate safe drinking habits
options.B: Leave all educational materials behind and only administer treatments quietly
options.C: Focus the entire talk on newborn baby care and breastfeeding techniques
options.D: Bring posters about snakebite prevention exclusively because they are colorful

explanation: Matching your materials to seasonal threats like cholera means your outreach hits right where help is needed most!

question: A patient scheduled for a sigmoidoscopy takes Warfarin daily for their heart. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to double their dose.
options.B: Notify the ordering doctor right away about the blood thinner.
options.C: Tell the patient to stop all meds forever.
options.D: Do the enema prep without mentioning the medication.

explanation: Safety first! Blood thinners raise the risk of bleeding if a biopsy is taken, so the doctor needs to review this beforehand.

question: Which detail is most important to include in the nursing documentation after the procedure?

options.A: The color of the bedsheets on the patient's bed
options.B: The names of all visiting family members present
options.C: The amount and character of gas or stool expelled
options.D: The exact brand name of the lubricant used

explanation: Documenting what was expelled helps the healthcare team evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention in relieving abdominal distention. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h6)

question: Where should a urinary drainage bag always hang relative to the patient's bladder?

options.A: Below the level of the bladder
options.B: Flat on the floor next to the bed
options.C: Above the level of the bladder
options.D: Level with the patient's chest

explanation: Always keep it lower than the bladder! Gravity keeps the urine flowing away from the body and stops nasty germs from creeping back up.

question: As a nurse working in adolescent health, which of these actions should you definitely NOT do?

options.A: Sharing a teenager's private health details with their neighbors
options.B: Screening for risky behaviors in a supportive, private setting
options.C: Providing confidential counseling on sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Educating on the correct use of modern contraceptive methods

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred! Gossiping or sharing private health info breaks professional ethics and destroys patient trust immediately.

question: What is the name of the layer of cells that clings directly to the released egg upon ovulation?

options.A: Zona pellucida
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Corona radiata
options.D: Myometrium

explanation: You got it! The corona radiata is a crown-like layer of follicular cells surrounding the egg that incoming sperm have to navigate through.

question: Which blood test results confirm primary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Low serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.B: Low serum calcium and high serum hormone
options.C: High serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.D: High serum calcium and high parathyroid hormone

explanation: In primary hyperparathyroidism, an overactive gland pumps out too much PTH, which in turn drives your blood calcium levels way up.

question: What are the two main parts that make up a patient's overall level of consciousness?

options.A: Speech and memory
options.B: Reflexes and coordination
options.C: Arousal and awareness
options.D: Strength and sensation

explanation: Consciousness is all about being awake (arousal) and being able to interact with your surroundings and thoughts (awareness). Both are essential!

question: How long does a released egg typically survive after ovulation if it doesn't meet a sperm?

options.A: 48 to 72 hours
options.B: 12 to 24 hours
options.C: 3 to 5 days
options.D: 1 week

explanation: An unfertilized egg has a surprisingly short lifespan! Once it leaves the ovary, it's only viable for about half a day to a full day.

question: A newly diagnosed patient is terrified to tell their partner because they fear physical abuse. What is your best nursing response?

options.A: Assist the client with safe disclosure planning and partner notification options
options.B: Tell the client to hide their medication and never mention the diagnosis
options.C: Advise the client to separate from the partner without any further discussion
options.D: Demand that the nurse call the spouse immediately without permission

explanation: Safety first, always! We help patients look at risks and use trained partner notification services that keep them safe.

question: Why should community health nurses team up with traditional birth attendants and local leaders?

options.A: To collect financial taxes from rural households
options.B: To stop all traditional practices permanently by force
options.C: To ensure coordinated care and prompt referral of dangerous cases
options.D: To hand over all clinical nursing duties to local leaders

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with local leaders builds strong community trust, ensuring that mothers with complications get rushed to the hospital safely and quickly.

question: Which physical reaction does the hypothalamus trigger during a fight-or-flight response?

options.A: Increased digestion
options.B: Increased heart rate
options.C: Narrowed airways
options.D: Slower breathing

explanation: Spot on! Stress hormones released via the hypothalamus make your heart beat faster to pump extra oxygen and blood to your muscles.
